A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RXNFLOW and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices A–D. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular-generation experiments on LIT-PCBA and CrossDocked2020, building-block ablations, and empirical subsampling-bias analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds results on 3D interaction modeling, baseline scaling, target specificity, MDP structure and generalization to structurally different building blocks.

M1.justification: V2 adds an experimental 3D variant using ligand–protein complex graphs with spatial edges and modified building-block scoring layers (Section 4.6; Appendix B.1). This extends the model, while the central action subsampling, joint reaction/block selection and trajectory-balance procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The principal datasets and targets remain unchanged. Appendices D.6–D.7 add nonaromatic-only building-block restrictions and structurally dissimilar unseen blocks with Tanimoto similarity below 0.5 to training blocks, extending the tested input conditions beyond v1's existing restrictions and random held-out blocks.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds DiffSBDD and MolCRAFT, including a larger-molecule MolCRAFT configuration. Figures 11–12 also add direct SynFlowNet and RGFN comparisons to the scaling investigations. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparisons; the newer SynFlowNet version discussed in Table 6 is not substituted into the main benchmarks.

E3.justification: New studies introduce controlled one-reaction, constant-reward timing experiments; a one-reaction 3D comparison using fast UniDock and Lipinski filtering; and top-10-molecule delta-score evaluation. Section 4.2 also changes the reported validity definition to Generation Success explicitly excluding disconnected molecules. This establishes a documented criterion change, without establishing that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct hierarchy ablation, structurally dissimilar-block generalization, comparative performance/runtime scaling, target-specificity analysis, property distributions and a 2D-versus-3D study. These test several previously unexamined aspects of the approach. V1's subsampling toy experiment is retained as Appendix D.8, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Table 13 newly reports Vina and QED means and standard deviations across five sample sets for pocket-conditional generation. Figure 7 reports standard errors over three seeds, and Figure 12 reports timing variability over 100 batches. Existing four-run reporting is retained; the PDFs do not establish an increased run count for existing experiments.

E6.justification: The original main benchmark values are retained, but substantial new results are added. Table 5 reports MolCRAFT-large at −9.25 Vina under its larger-atom setting, while RXNFLOW remains −8.85. Table 14 adds delta scores, including −1.13 for both RXNFLOW and TacoGFN. New figures report scaling, robustness, generalization and 3D-model findings.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds mathematical edge-flow parameterizations for the 3D variant in Equations 29–30. This is a limited formal addition: the GFlowNet foundations and Appendix A bias/variance derivations and proofs remain unchanged apart from cross-references.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims about scalable synthesis-oriented generation, diversity, synthesizability and adaptation without retraining. The headline CrossDocked2020 results and state-of-the-art claims are also retained.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the best-docking-score interpretation with a competitive comparison against MolCRAFT-large while emphasizing drug-likeness. New Section 4.6 discusses spatial interaction information and the exploration imposed by uniform subsampling, identifying prioritized sampling as a possible improvement.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project source-code link, explicit TacoGFN reward details, disclosure of retrosynthetic enumeration for valid backward trajectories, and provenance for the added baselines' samples. It also documents the 3D experiment's implementation settings. Most existing hardware, hyperparameters and data-processing information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B.5 substantially expands comparison with the closest prior methods, distinguishing two SynFlowNet versions through backward-trajectory handling, action embeddings and sampling costs. Added references cover MolCRAFT, target specificity, synthesizable chemical-space generation, negative sampling and REINFORCE. Bibliographic updates to existing works are separate from this substantive positioning expansion.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. V2 adds Section 4.6, reorganizes and expands appendices B and D, relocates Algorithm 1 to Appendix B.4, and makes localized terminology, cross-reference, acknowledgement and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds extensive diagnostic displays, including property-distribution panels, scaling curves, 3D learning curves, robustness plots and Tables 13–14. Tables 5–6 expand, Figures 1–3 are redrawn, and Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix. Several older appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central efficiency and adaptability claims through comparative scaling, direct hierarchy ablation and structurally dissimilar-block tests that v1 lacked. Uncertainty reporting and broader baselines further improve the evidence. The unchanged headline state-of-the-art Vina claim still needs qualification given MolCRAFT-large's different atom-count setting, but this limitation does not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
